CV Rewrite

A CV that fits the job. Not a template with your name in it.

Paste your current CV and the job advert. Answer a few short questions where we spot the gaps. Get back a CV rewritten to align with this specific role, in a design you choose. Downloads as Word and PDF.

Free, always  No card. No subscription. No catch.

Rewrite my CV Read the free CV guide →

About 10 minutes to fill in. Your rewritten CV is usually ready in under 2 minutes.

21 designs, two styles

Real designs, not templates

A few of the layouts you can choose from, each rendered from a real CV and downloadable as Word or PDF.

What you actually get

Every CV is built fresh from your CV and the actual advert, not a generic layout everyone gets. Written in your own words where it matters, tailored to one role, checked for honesty before it reaches you.

A tailored rewrite. Your CV re-aligned to this specific advert, mirroring its language where you genuinely have the experience.

A gap check first. We compare the advert against your CV line by line and only ask about what's genuinely missing.

The seven stops, done properly. Header, personal statement, key skills with proof, career history, interests, education, and the skills-match answer key.

A personal statement that sounds like you. Built from your own words, never buzzword salad.

Key skills with receipts. Each skill paired with a short prove-it line: what you did, what happened.

A fabrication check. Every figure and claim is traced back to something you actually told us. Nothing invented, no inflated numbers.

21 designs, two styles. Sixteen editable Word/ATS layouts plus five premium designer PDFs, so two people using this never walk out with the same document.

Word and PDF. Plus an ATS-safe version for application portals, on request.

Before & after

Same person, two CVs. One is the generic, buzzword-stuffed version everyone ends up with. The other is rewritten to the advert from real facts, honesty-checked and properly designed. That is the difference.

Illustrative example. Your rewrite uses only your own facts, never invented ones.

How it works

1

Paste your CV and the advert

Upload a file or paste the text, either works. The advert can be a link too.

2

Answer a few questions

We read both documents, spot where your CV is thin against the role, and only ask what's needed. Type it, or just talk and we'll transcribe it.

3

We rewrite, then check it

Section by section, in your own words. Then a fabrication check makes sure nothing was invented or inflated.

4

Choose a design, download

Pick from 21 designs across two styles, preview it, download as Word and PDF. ATS-safe version on request.

Free. Every CV, every time.

CV Rewrite used to cost a few pounds. Now it costs nothing, for everyone, every time. Tailor your CV to one job or to twenty. Sign in with your email so your work is there when you come back.

£0

Every CV

Rewrite for as many roles as you're going for. No packs, no credits, no card details.

21

Designs

Every design and every format included: Word, PDF and the ATS-safe version.

Why free? Because a good CV shouldn't depend on what's in your bank account. Comquat comes from The Com'mon People, and like every guide, dispatch and Loudspeaker there, it's free.

Rewrite my CV

No subscription. No catch.

Most CV builders lock you into a monthly subscription, often after a cheap trial that quietly renews. We don't. Ours is free. That's it.

Comquat

  • Free, every CV, every time
  • No subscription. Nothing auto-renews, ever
  • No card details, ever
  • Written to your exact job advert, in your own words
  • Honesty check: nothing invented, no inflated numbers
  • Word, PDF and an ATS-safe version all included

Typical CV subscriptions

  • Around £15 to £30 a month, billed until you cancel
  • Often a £2 "trial" that rolls into the full price
  • Charged whether you used it that month or not
  • Frequently generic templates, not advert-specific
  • Little or no check on invented claims
  • Some formats or features locked to higher tiers

The "typical" figures are the common range across popular résumé subscription tools in 2026. Other tools' prices change; ours is zero.

Rewrite my CV

Questions

Is this actually AI, or a template with my name stuck in?

It's a real rewrite built from your specific CV and the actual advert each time, not a fixed template. We use AI to tidy grammar and sharpen your sentences, never to write your personal statement or career story in its own voice. If we can't ground something in what you told us, we say so plainly rather than filling it with filler.

Will it make things up to sound impressive?

No, and we built a hard check specifically to stop that. Every number, employer, title, qualification and skill in the finished CV has to trace back to something you actually provided. Anything that doesn't gets stripped out and shown to you as a question to answer, not quietly left in.

Is my data safe?

Uploaded files are deleted from our server as soon as the text has been pulled out. Same policy as Comquat Interview Prep.

What's the ATS version?

Online application portals parse your CV with software before a human sees it. The ATS version strips your chosen design down to a single column with standard headings, no tables, no icons and no header or footer, so it parses cleanly. You get it from the same design you picked.

Is it really free?

Yes. Every CV, every design, every format, every time. No credits, no card, no trial that turns into a bill. The only thing The Com'mon People still charges for is an optional one-to-one coaching session with a real person.

Do I need an account?

Yes, a light one. You sign in with your email, we send you a link, no password to remember. That's how your work follows you between visits.

What if something's not right after I've downloaded?

You can tweak the Word file yourself, it's yours. If the service genuinely failed to give you a usable CV, get in touch and we'll put it right.

Why give it away?

Because Comquat comes from The Com'mon People, which is built on mutual aid. Every guide, dispatch and Loudspeaker email is free, always, and now the tools that do the work for you are too.

Why people use it

✓

Honest by design

A hard fabrication check means nothing gets invented or inflated. Every claim traces back to something you told us.

✓

Sounds like a person

The usual AI tells - "I was drawn to", "proven track record", "passionate about" - are banned. Plain English, in your voice.

✓

No subscription trap

It's free. Nothing to buy, nothing to renew, nothing to cancel.

From the founder

Why I built this

After nine years in recruitment, I found myself on the other side of the desk, job-hunting like everyone else.

So I built myself two small tools. One to rewrite my CV for the exact role I was going for, digging out the real things I'd done that made me right for it. And one to get me ready for the interview. A week later, I'd landed the job.

Turns out it isn't complicated. It just helps to have a hand. So we turned those two tools into Comquat, free for anyone who needs it.

Same tools. Your turn. · Neil

Ready when you are

Paste your CV and the advert. We'll do the rest.

Rewrite my CV

Comquat is the free CV Rewrite and Interview Prep app from The Com'mon People, the free resource centre for both sides of recruitment. Built on mutual aid.

CV Rewrite · Comquat

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 17 November 2026

This policy explains what happens to your information when you use Comquat CV Rewrite at cv.the-common-people.com. We keep it plain, and we keep your data for as little time as we can.

Who we are

Comquat CV Rewrite is run by Comquat Ventures UK Ltd, a private limited company registered in England and Wales (company number 17581616). Comquat is the CV Rewrite and Interview Prep app from The Com'mon People. We are the "data controller" for the information described here.

Contact for any privacy question or request: neil.copping@thecommonpeople.co.uk.
Post: Comquat Ventures UK Ltd, 102 Stevenage Road, Hitchin, SG4 9DQ (our registered office).

What we collect

  • The CV and job advert you upload or paste.
  • Any answers you give to our questions, typed or recorded by voice, and any answers you give for a cover letter.
  • A photo, only if you choose to add one to your CV.
  • Your name and email address, held in your Comquat account so you can sign in (see Your Comquat account below), and used, if you ask, to email your finished CV to you.
  • A record that you ticked the box to confirm you'd checked your CV or cover letter before downloading it.
  • Any feedback you choose to leave: a star rating and an optional comment.
  • One essential session cookie (see Cookies below).

Your CV will contain personal information such as your name, contact details and work history. Please leave out anything you wouldn't want processed, and avoid special category data (for example health or ethnicity) unless it is genuinely needed for the role.

Do you have to give us this? No. But we need your CV and the job advert to rewrite your CV, and an email address if you want an account. Without them, we can't do that part for you.

Why we use it, and our legal basis

  • To rewrite your CV, build your skills match report, and let you preview and download the result. This is necessary to provide the service you asked for.
  • To transcribe a voice answer, only if you choose to record one. This is based on your consent, and you can always type instead.
  • To sign you in and email you your CV. This is necessary to provide the service.
  • To read your feedback and improve the app. This is our legitimate interest in making Comquat better.

Your Comquat account

A free Comquat account gives you one sign-in for CV Rewrite and Interview Prep. If you create one, we keep:

  • Your name and email address, so you can sign in and we know what to call you.
  • Your password, if you set one, stored only as a scrambled one-way code. We can't see it. You can sign in with an email link instead.
  • Your email choices: which of our newsletters and updates you've ticked, plus a record of when you ticked or unticked each one.
  • Your download confirmations: a record, with the date and time, each time you tick the box to say you've checked your CV or cover letter before downloading it.
  • Your saved documents: a copy of each CV, cover letter and interview prep report you download while signed in, so you can download it again from your account page. Each one holds whatever is in the document, such as your name, contact details and work history.
  • Your master CV, if you build one: everything you type, say or tick in it, such as your name, contact details, your answers to the questions, work history, skills and qualifications, plus the writing style and design you pick and any sample of your own writing you paste in, so you can come back to it and tailor it for each job.
  • When you joined and when you last signed in.

As we add features, your account will also hold an optional profile with a photo. We'll update this notice before that goes live.

Why, and our legal basis. We use your account details, your master CV and your saved documents to provide the account you asked for (contract). We keep your download confirmations because we have a legitimate interest in being able to show you checked your documents yourself before using them. We only send you the newsletters and updates you've ticked (consent), and you can untick them at any time from your account page.

Where it's kept. Your account, your master CV and your saved documents are stored with Supabase, in their London data centre. Only you can see them, and there are no public links to your documents. We only look at your account to help when you ask us to, or to fix a problem.

AI and your details. Nothing in your account (your name, email, password, email choices, master CV or saved documents) is sent to an AI service unless you ask for it, in one of three ways:

  • If you press Write it up for me or Turn this into CV points in the CV builder, the answers or notes for that part are sent to Anthropic to write them up in the style you picked. Your personal details are taken out first.
  • If you record an answer instead of typing, the recording goes to OpenAI as it is, to be turned into text. We don't keep the recording. If you'd rather it didn't go, type instead.
  • If you choose to tailor your master CV for a job, it goes into CV Rewrite like any other CV, and your personal details are taken out before the AI sees it.

See How we keep your details from the AI below for how the details are taken out.

How long we keep it. Until you delete it. You can delete any saved document or your master CV on its own, or your whole account, from your account page at any time, and it's removed straight away. We also take you off the Comquat emails you ticked. If you signed up to The Loudspeaker or anything else separately on our website, that stays as it is, and you can unsubscribe using the link in any email. If you don't use your account for three years, we'll email you a month before closing your account, and then delete it.

How we keep your details from the AI

Before your CV, your answers or anything else you give us goes to the AI, we take out your name, email address, phone number, home address and postcode, website and social media links, and date of birth. We swap each one for a placeholder, such as [NAME]. The AI only ever sees the placeholders. When its work comes back, we put your real details back in before you see it.

We can only take out details we can recognise, so please leave out anything else personal that the job doesn't need, such as your referees' contact details. If you record a voice answer, the recording goes to OpenAI as it is to be turned into text, so if you'd rather it didn't, type your answer instead.

No decisions made by computer. We don't make any decisions about you using automated means. The AI drafts your CV, skills match report or interview prep for you to check and change, and you decide what to do with them.

Who processes your data for us

We use a small number of trusted service providers ("processors"), who act only on our instructions:

  • Anthropic: the AI that reads your CV and the advert, rewrites your CV, builds your skills match report and, when you ask, writes up your answers in the CV builder, working on a copy with your personal details taken out (see above).
  • OpenAI: turns a voice answer into text, only if you record one.
  • Supabase: stores your Comquat account, your master CV and your saved documents, and handles signing in, in their London data centre.
  • Resend: sends your sign-in emails, your finished CV if you ask, and any newsletters you've ticked.
  • Render: hosts the app.

Some of these providers are based in the United States. Where your data is transferred outside the UK, it is protected by appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses. We do not sell your data, and we do not use it to train AI models.

CV Rewrite is free and we don't take payments for it. If that ever changes, we'll update this policy before any payment is taken.

How long we keep it

  • Uploaded files are deleted from our server as soon as the text has been read out of them.
  • Your CV, advert, answers, photo and skills match report are held only for your working session (up to three hours) so you can tweak and re-download, then discarded. If you're signed in to a Comquat account, a copy of each CV and cover letter you download is kept in your account until you delete it (see Your Comquat account above). Otherwise we don't keep a copy.
  • Your Comquat account is kept until you delete it, or until it has gone unused for three years (see Your Comquat account above).
  • Feedback is kept so we can learn from it. Ask us and we'll delete yours.
  • Emails we send you may stay in our email system as a record.

Your rights

Under UK data protection law you have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict or object to its use, to data portability, and to withdraw consent at any time. If you have a Comquat account, you can download everything it holds, correct your name and delete the account yourself from your account page. For anything else, email us at the address above. Unless you've saved documents to a Comquat account, we delete your CV data quickly, so there may be little left to act on once your session has ended.

If you're unhappy with how we've handled your data, tell us first by emailing the address above with "Data protection complaint" in the subject line. We'll confirm we've got it within 30 days, and keep you posted while we look into it. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

Cookies

We use one essential "session" cookie so the app can remember your progress while you use it. If you sign in to a Comquat account, we also use essential sign-in cookies that keep you signed in across CV Rewrite and Interview Prep. We don't use tracking, analytics or advertising cookies, so there's nothing to opt into.

Security

The app runs over an encrypted (HTTPS) connection and we limit how long your data exists. No system is perfectly secure, but we take reasonable steps to protect your information.

Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The "last updated" date at the top shows when it last changed.

Read our Terms and Conditions →

© 2026 Comquat, from The Com'mon People. Built on mutual aid. Privacy · Terms

Your master CV

Let's build your CV.

No experience? No problem. Talk or type your answers, tick what sounds like you, and watch your CV build itself as you go. It saves as you work, and only you can see it.

  • 1Talk or type
  • 2Tick what sounds like you
  • 3Watch it build
0%done

Sign in to build your CV

The CV builder comes free with a Comquat account. Sign in, then open it from My account.

Create my free account Sign in

Loading your CV…

1 About you

Name at the top, how to reach you right under it. Recruiters shouldn't have to hunt.

2 Your story

This is the first thing they read about you. Be a person, not a press release. Answer the questions in your own words. Typing not your thing? Press the microphone and just talk. School, college, caring for someone, sport, volunteering and the things you love all count.

How should your CV sound?

Or match my own writing style

Paste a paragraph or two you've written yourself, like a message, a bio or a bit of homework. We'll copy how you sound (your tone, not your content).

See what good looks like

Avoid: "A creative, structured professional with the ability to engage with customers in both effective and impactful ways."

Do this: "I'm a marketer who learned the trade running events for my mum's café. Twelve years on, I still believe the best campaigns start with knowing one customer properly. I work best in honest teams. My border collie thinks I should retire and walk her more."

From The Com'mon People CV guide. Specific, warm and memorable, and it sounds like a real person.

About "Write it up for me": it uses AI to turn your answers into a statement in the style you picked. It only uses what you told us, and your name and contact details are taken out first. Always read it back and change anything that doesn't sound like you.

3 Key skills and behaviours

Tap the ones that sound like you. Each one becomes a strength on your CV, written for you. Be honest: the best CVs sound like the person. Eight to twelve works best.

Nothing picked yet

Skills you can prove

Name the skill, then one line that proves it: what you did, and what came of it. "Cash handling: cashed up the till every Saturday for a year" beats "good with money".

Stuck? Ideas for skills you can prove
  • Customer service: served 200 covers on a Saturday shift; regulars asked for me by name.
  • Cash handling: cashed up the till every closing shift for a year without a discrepancy.
  • Looking after people: cared for my grandad after his stroke, managing his medication and appointments.
  • Organising: planned our Year 11 prom for 120 students, including the budget and the DJ.
  • Leading a team: captain of the under-16s for two seasons; set up the training rota.
  • Digital skills: built and ran the Instagram page for my aunt's bakery.
  • Languages: fluent in Polish; translated for customers at my Saturday job.
  • Practical skills: rebuilt two bikes from parts and now fix friends' bikes.

Only write what's true for you. Small, real proof beats big, vague claims.

4 Experience

First CV, or no paid work yet? That's fine. Saturday jobs, work experience, volunteering, caring for family, running a club or team, a fundraiser or a big project at school or college all count. "Organised a bake sale that raised £240 for the hospice" is real experience.

Latest first. Just tell us about it in your own words, typed or spoken, then press Turn this into CV points. Or write the points yourself.

Stuck? Ideas for what to say

What did you do? Served, cooked, cleaned, cashed up, greeted, answered, restocked, delivered, looked after, trained, organised, planned, fixed, built, sold, set up, ran, sorted, checked, helped new starters.

What came of it?

  • Something you were praised, thanked or trusted with ("Trusted to open up on my own after three months").
  • Something that got better because of you.
  • Numbers: money raised, people served, hours worked, days without missing a shift.
  • Anything new you learned or were given more responsibility for.

Reasons for leaving that read well: went back to college, moved house, a better opportunity, the job was seasonal, the contract ended, left to care for family. Still there? Leave it blank.

5 Education and training

Where, what, when and, if they're good, what you got. Certificates and short courses count too. On a first CV, this is where you make your case, so use it.

Stuck? Ideas for what counts
  • GCSEs: list your subjects and grades, or say "9 GCSEs including English and Maths".
  • A levels, BTECs, T Levels, NVQs and diplomas, with grades if you have them.
  • Apprenticeships and traineeships, finished or in progress.
  • Food Hygiene Level 2, First Aid, Manual Handling, Fire Marshal.
  • Driving licence, CSCS card, Personal Licence, forklift licence.
  • Duke of Edinburgh, Prince's Trust, National Citizen Service, Scouts or Guides awards.
  • Online courses you finished, such as Google, OpenLearn or FutureLearn.
  • Still studying? Put "Expected" and the date.

6 Interests

Underrated and powerful. Interests are how a stranger finds a reason to like you before you've met. Be specific ("netball for a local team" beats "sport") and be real. Three to six is plenty, one per line.

Tap an idea to add it, then make it yours: say which team, which games, which cause.

7 Pick a look and download

Pick the look you like best. You'll see it straight away in the preview. The PDF is ready to send. Want to change the wording yourself? Download Word. Every download is saved in My documents.

Applying through an online form? Use the ATS-safe PDF: it's plain and easy for application systems to read. Word versions use a simpler layout so they're easy to edit.

More designs (the same ones as CV Rewrite)

Got a job in mind?

Press Tailor it for a job. CV Rewrite starts with this CV already filled in, in the style you picked, and matches it to the advert. Apply for the two jobs you really want, not fifty.

Interview Prep · Comquat

Privacy & Data Notice

Last updated: 17 November 2026

Who we are

Comquat Interview Prep builds a personalised interview preparation report from the job description and CV you give us. It's run by Comquat Ventures UK Ltd, a private limited company registered in England and Wales (company number 17581616). Comquat is the CV Rewrite and Interview Prep app from The Com'mon People. We are the "data controller" for the information described here.

Contact for any privacy question or request: neil.copping@thecommonpeople.co.uk.
Post: Comquat Ventures UK Ltd, 102 Stevenage Road, Hitchin, SG4 9DQ (our registered office).

What we collect

DataWhy we collect it
Your name, email address, and the company and role you're applying forTo personalise your report and opening pitch, and to keep a record that you agreed to this notice before we generated anything
Your CV and the job description (uploaded file or pasted text)To research the company, work out your skills match and gaps, and draft your pitch, STAR answers and questions
Spoken answers, if you choose to record them (audio, then turned into text)To draft your answers in your own words. The audio goes to our transcription provider and isn't kept by us afterwards
Whether you've opted in to hearing from usA separate, optional tick-box, kept apart from your agreement to this notice. You can withdraw it at any time
Your name, email and chosen time, if you book a coaching callTo arrange and confirm your session

Do you have to give us this? No. But we need the job description, and your name and email, to build your report. Without them, we can't make it.

Our legal basis

  • Building your report, and arranging a coaching call if you book one, is necessary to provide the service you asked for.
  • Recording a voice answer, and hearing from us about future guides and tools, are based on your consent. Both are optional.

How long we keep it

  • Uploaded CV and job description files are deleted from our server as soon as the text has been read out of them.
  • Recorded audio is deleted as soon as it has been transcribed.
  • Your report isn't stored after it's been sent to your browser, apart from what's needed to build your downloadable document in the same request. If you're signed in to a Comquat account, a copy of the Word document is kept in your account until you delete it (see Your Comquat account below).
  • Your name, email, and the record that you agreed to this notice (plus whether you opted in to hearing from us) are kept as evidence of consent. You can ask us to delete them at any time.
  • Coaching booking details are kept until the session has taken place, plus a short period afterwards for any follow-up.

Your Comquat account

A free Comquat account gives you one sign-in for CV Rewrite and Interview Prep. If you create one, we keep:

  • Your name and email address, so you can sign in and we know what to call you.
  • Your password, if you set one, stored only as a scrambled one-way code. We can't see it. You can sign in with an email link instead.
  • Your email choices: which of our newsletters and updates you've ticked, plus a record of when you ticked or unticked each one.
  • Your download confirmations: a record, with the date and time, each time you tick the box to say you've checked your CV or cover letter before downloading it.
  • Your saved documents: a copy of each CV, cover letter and interview prep report you download while signed in, so you can download it again from your account page. Each one holds whatever is in the document, such as your name, contact details and work history.
  • Your master CV, if you build one: everything you type, say or tick in it, such as your name, contact details, your answers to the questions, work history, skills and qualifications, plus the writing style and design you pick and any sample of your own writing you paste in, so you can come back to it and tailor it for each job.
  • When you joined and when you last signed in.

As we add features, your account will also hold an optional profile with a photo. We'll update this notice before that goes live.

Why, and our legal basis. We use your account details, your master CV and your saved documents to provide the account you asked for (contract). We keep your download confirmations because we have a legitimate interest in being able to show you checked your documents yourself before using them. We only send you the newsletters and updates you've ticked (consent), and you can untick them at any time from your account page.

Where it's kept. Your account, your master CV and your saved documents are stored with Supabase, in their London data centre. Only you can see them, and there are no public links to your documents. We only look at your account to help when you ask us to, or to fix a problem.

AI and your details. Nothing in your account (your name, email, password, email choices, master CV or saved documents) is sent to an AI service unless you ask for it, in one of three ways:

  • If you press Write it up for me or Turn this into CV points in the CV builder, the answers or notes for that part are sent to Anthropic to write them up in the style you picked. Your personal details are taken out first.
  • If you record an answer instead of typing, the recording goes to OpenAI as it is, to be turned into text. We don't keep the recording. If you'd rather it didn't go, type instead.
  • If you choose to tailor your master CV for a job, it goes into CV Rewrite like any other CV, and your personal details are taken out before the AI sees it.

See How we keep your details from the AI below for how the details are taken out.

How long we keep it. Until you delete it. You can delete any saved document or your master CV on its own, or your whole account, from your account page at any time, and it's removed straight away. We also take you off the Comquat emails you ticked. If you signed up to The Loudspeaker or anything else separately on our website, that stays as it is, and you can unsubscribe using the link in any email. If you don't use your account for three years, we'll email you a month before closing your account, and then delete it.

How we keep your details from the AI

Before your CV, your answers or anything else you give us goes to the AI, we take out your name, email address, phone number, home address and postcode, website and social media links, and date of birth. We swap each one for a placeholder, such as [NAME]. The AI only ever sees the placeholders. When its work comes back, we put your real details back in before you see it.

We can only take out details we can recognise, so please leave out anything else personal that the job doesn't need, such as your referees' contact details. If you record a voice answer, the recording goes to OpenAI as it is to be turned into text, so if you'd rather it didn't, type your answer instead.

No decisions made by computer. We don't make any decisions about you using automated means. The AI drafts your CV, skills match report or interview prep for you to check and change, and you decide what to do with them.

Who processes your data for us

We use a small number of trusted service providers. None of them may use your data for their own purposes.

ProviderWhat they see
Anthropic (Claude)Your job description and CV text, with your personal details taken out first (see above), to research the company and draft your report
OpenAIYour spoken answers (to turn them into text) and a short description of the role (to create your report's cover artwork)
SupabaseYour Comquat account, master CV and saved documents, if you have an account, stored in their London data centre
ResendYour name and email, to send booking confirmations, sign-in emails and any newsletters you've ticked, and to let us know a report has been requested
StripePayment for a coaching call, if you book one. We never see or store your card details
RenderHosting-level access to run the app

Some of these providers are based in the United States. Where your data is transferred outside the UK, it is protected by appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses. We don't sell your data, and we don't use it to train AI models.

The interview prep report itself is free. The only thing we charge for is the optional coaching call.

Your rights

Under UK data protection law you have the right to access, correct or ask us to delete the personal data we hold about you, to object to or restrict certain processing, to data portability, and to withdraw consent at any time. If you have a Comquat account, you can download everything it holds, correct your name and delete the account yourself from your account page. For anything else, email us at the address above. If you're unhappy with how we've handled your data, tell us first by emailing the address above with "Data protection complaint" in the subject line. We'll confirm we've got it within 30 days, and keep you posted while we look into it. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

Security

Uploaded files are checked for size and type before they're accepted, and deleted as soon as they've been read. Access to hosting and provider accounts is limited to the people who need it to run the service.

Cookies

If you sign in to a Comquat account, we use essential sign-in cookies that keep you signed in across Interview Prep and CV Rewrite. This app doesn't use tracking or advertising cookies.

Changes to this notice

We may update this notice as the service develops. Any change will be shown here with a new "last updated" date.

A Real Sample Report

See What You Get. Free.

This isn't a mock-up. It's a real report, built by Comquat Interview Prep, our free app, for a real interview - Neil Copping (our founder) preparing to interview for Recruitment Manager at the Royal Albert Hall. We've published it in full, sources and all, so you can see exactly what your own report will look like.

11Report Sections
25Sources Cited
62%Skills Match Scored
<2 MinTo Generate
Get Your Own Report, Free
Every section below is reproduced from Neil's actual report, generated 23 July 2026. Company names, figures and sources are all real and correct as of that date - this is exactly the standard of research your own report is built to.
01 · Company Overview

The Royal Albert Hall

A 150-year-old, publicly-facing charity, not a commercial venue business - that distinction matters for how you should frame your pitch.

The Royal Albert Hall is legally The Corporation of the Hall of Arts and Sciences, a registered charity (number 254543) held in trust for the nation, with a charitable purpose to promote the Arts and Sciences and preserve its Grade I listed building. It receives no public subsidy for running costs, which is unusual for a major UK cultural institution and shapes how commercially-minded the culture actually is.

Headcount is around 525 employees according to the Hall's own governance page, led by a Chief Executive and Executive team who report to a board of Trustees - a notably lean structure for an organisation hosting the volume of activity it does.

Scale of activity: roughly 400 events in the main auditorium plus around 1,000 events in other spaces each year, with nearly 2 million people enjoying experiences in the building annually, and millions more reached via broadcast and online.

Funding model is unusual and worth understanding before interview: the Hall was originally built by selling seat rights to "Members" (Seatholders) who still pay an annual seat rate today. The 2024 annual report shows total income of £60.5m (up from £54.4m in 2023) against expenditure of £47.0m, producing a net surplus of £12.2m.

There's a live piece of legislation, the Royal Albert Hall Bill, working through Parliament - it passed its Third Reading in the House of Lords in January 2025 after a contested Opposed Bill Committee process in 2024 concerning the Hall's governance structure. This is a genuinely live governance issue, not ancient history, and worth being aware of if it comes up.

Leadership: CEO is James Ainscough OBE, who rejoined in spring 2023 after previously serving the Hall from 2008 to 2017, then five years as CEO of the charity Help Musicians, where he oversaw distribution of £20m in pandemic hardship funding.

The Hall is mid-way through a major capital programme called the Estate Plan, covering £73m of maintenance work and £261m of proposed capital projects over 15 years - a rethink of the original "Great Restoration" plan after Covid changed the Hall's financial position.

There isn't a direct commercial competitor in the way a normal business would have one. Its closest peers are other major UK cultural and heritage venues (Southbank Centre, Barbican, London Coliseum), but its real USP is the building itself: a Grade I listed, purpose-built 1871 venue with genuine global brand recognition, hosting everything from the BBC Proms to boxing to graduations.

Sourced from: Royal Albert Hall governance pages, the Corporation's FY24 Annual Report and Accounts, Royal Albert Hall press releases, Arts Professional, The Org, IQ Magazine, RICS Modus, Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
02 · Recent News & Press Activity

What's actually been happening

Coverage is steady but venue and programming-focused rather than corporate - expect trade press (IQ Magazine, Arts Professional) rather than mainstream business news.

July 2025: CEO James Ainscough set out a three-point strategic vision for the Hall in an interview with IQ Magazine, tying the Hall's approach to a voluntary £1 grassroots music levy scheme and confirming the Hall was hosting the 2025 BBC Proms season, alongside newly announced associate artists Rushil Ranjan and Abi Sampa.

January 2025: the Royal Albert Hall Bill passed its Third Reading in the House of Lords, following a 2024 Opposed Bill Committee hearing triggered by a petition from a former President of the Hall. The Committee ultimately found the petitioners lacked standing, but issued a Special Report flagging governance concerns to Parliament and the Government.

March 2025 (International Women's Day): the Hall partnered with WOW - Women of the World to mark WOW's 15th anniversary, part of its continuing programming push around EDI and diverse headliners.

The Hall continues to publicly report strong financials, suggesting the organisation is in a growth phase post-pandemic rather than contraction.

No major leadership churn has been reported since Ainscough's 2023 appointment, and no reported departures at Executive team level in recent coverage.

There is limited fresh, dated news specific to HR, recruitment or People & Culture team changes - most recent coverage centres on programming, governance and the Estate Plan, so don't expect the interviewer to reference recent press about their own function.

Sourced from: IQ Magazine, Royal Albert Hall press office, RICS Modus, Arts Professional.
03 · Employee Sentiment

What people who work there actually say

Mixed-to-average marks on the numbers, with career progression flagged as the weakest area - worth probing tactfully rather than raising as an accusation.

Glassdoor shows 71 reviews for the Royal Albert Hall, and employees rate career opportunities at 2.8 out of 5 based on 91 anonymous ratings - the softest sub-metric found, and worth a gentle, curious interview question about internal mobility and progression frameworks, which ties directly into this job's remit around building "a structured and transparent framework for talent management and promotion."

Compensation and benefits fared better: Glassdoor's salary data (146 submitted salaries) shows employees rate comp and benefits at 3.5 out of 5, consistent with the fairly generous staff benefits package the Hall advertises (25 days annual leave plus buy/sell, 6x salary life assurance, enhanced family leave).

Given the review volume for an organisation of around 525 staff, this is a reasonably representative sample, not a handful of outliers - so the career-progression score is a real signal, and lines up with the job description's own admission that this is a known, self-acknowledged gap you're being hired partly to help fix.

No detailed qualitative review text could be confirmed from the sources found - be cautious about repeating secondhand claims about specific manager or team complaints in the interview; stick to what's verifiable.

Sourced from: Glassdoor company reviews, Glassdoor salary data, Royal Albert Hall careers page.
04 · Social Media Presence

How they actually show up online

LinkedIn is where recruitment and leadership news actually gets posted - the January 2023 announcement of James Ainscough's CEO appointment drew visible engagement including congratulatory comments from industry peers.

The Hall's main channels are built around its performance programme rather than employer-branding content, with a celebratory, heritage-driven tone ("icons grace our stage" is a recurring phrase), which tells you a lot about how they'll want careers content pitched too.

Given the job description explicitly tasks this role with working alongside Marketing on employer brand activity and careers content, it's worth having a view in interview on how the Hall's current, heavily programming-led social presence could be extended into genuine careers content - because right now that gap is visible from the outside.

Sourced from: Royal Albert Hall LinkedIn, Instagram and public social channels.
05 · Market & Sector Intelligence

What's putting pressure on this industry right now

This role sits at the intersection of two live pressures: the UK charity and arts sector's tight labour market for specialist operational and creative talent, and a live capital transformation programme that will keep hiring volume and complexity high for years.

The Hall is mid-programme on its Estate Plan, meaning sustained recruitment demand across Building Services, project management and technical/estates roles for the foreseeable future, not a one-off spike.

The job spec itself lists Philanthropy, Building Services, IT and Visitor Services as functions this one Recruitment Manager will need to flex across - a broader sector reality, as arts and heritage charities compete for both commercial skillsets (finance, IT, fundraising) and specialist or front-of-house skillsets, often against very different pay benchmarks.

As a charity with no public subsidy for running costs, every recruitment agency fee and advertising spend line is scrutinised, lining up directly with the job description's explicit requirement to control agency and advertising spend for value for money.

EDI has moved from marketing language to an audited strategic objective here - the pack names building the Hall's reputation as a "Force For Good" as one of four Strategic Objectives, and CEO James Ainscough is on record saying there is "much still to do." Expect this interviewer to test whether you can operationalise inclusive recruitment practically, not just recite the value.

Sector-wide, arts and heritage organisations are increasingly competing with commercial employers for HR and recruitment specialists who can bring ATS and data discipline - the job explicitly wants Dayforce experience, signalling the Hall knows it's playing catch-up on recruitment technology maturity relative to more corporate sectors.

Sourced from: RICS Modus, Royal Albert Hall recruitment pack, sector reporting.
06 · Challenges You May Be Facing

The honest version, not the job-ad version

This is a two-person team carrying strategic and highly operational load simultaneously, in a building where seasonal peaks and specialist, rare roles both spike volume and complexity at once.

You'll be building infrastructure, not just running an existing process - the pack explicitly frames this as a newly created position meant to bring structure, insight and a focus on continuous improvement, meaning you likely won't inherit a mature playbook.

Team capacity is genuinely thin: one direct report plus you, covering end-to-end recruitment and onboarding across the entire Hall, including personally covering day-to-day recruitment administration when your colleague is on leave.

Volume and variety will be a live operational challenge - high-volume seasonal roles alongside highly specialist or senior hires, each needing a different sourcing and assessment approach.

Compliance load is heavy and non-negotiable - right-to-work, DBS, Occupational Health, referencing and GDPR all sit under this role, and given the Hall's public-facing, high-footfall nature, the reputational cost of a compliance failure here is higher than in a typical back-office business.

System maturity is a real gap to walk in aware of - Dayforce experience is listed as desirable rather than essential, which suggests current systems and data flow between recruitment and HR/payroll are not yet fully embedded. A sensible interview question is to ask directly how mature the current ATS-to-Dayforce data flow actually is today.

The career-progression sentiment and the job pack's own commitment to a transparent talent framework point to the same tension: retention and internal mobility are acknowledged weak spots, and part of what you're being hired to fix sits upstream of recruitment (attraction, employer brand, inclusive process design) rather than purely downstream.

07 · Your Opening Pitch

The Pitch Sandwich

Built from Neil's real CV and answers, weighted to this specific role.

Bread 1 · Connect

A bit about me - I'm Neil Copping, I live in Hitchin.

Filling · Fit

Professionally, I've spent nearly nine years running full-cycle recruitment at Tate across HR, Marketing, Finance, Tech, Creative and Operations briefs, handling everything from briefing through to offer, building candidate pipelines from scratch, and managing the ATS daily with responsibility for right-to-work checks, referencing and GDPR compliance on every placement. I've also line-managed a team of up to three consultants with regular one-to-ones and performance reviews, sat on Tate's EDI strategy team shaping inclusive hiring practices, and worked directly with employers on apprenticeship recruitment and levy conversations alongside Amazing Apprenticeships. That combination of high-volume delivery, hands-on process ownership and inclusive recruitment experience maps closely onto what this role needs, and I've done it while managing agency-side PSL relationships, which gives me a useful perspective on how to run those arrangements from the client side too.

Bread 2 · Values

In how I work, I value honesty, which means you'll get someone who tells a hiring manager the truth about a shortlist even when it's not what they want to hear, who flags a broken process instead of quietly working around it, and who'd rather under-promise on a time-to-hire than dress up a number to make a report look good.

08 · Gap Analysis

The Cake + Cherry Method

Skills Match62%

8 of 13 job requirements matched directly to Neil's CV.

Matched strengths

Nearly nine years of full-cycle, end-to-end recruitment across HR, Marketing, Finance, Tech, Creative and Operations briefs.

Line management and coaching experience, having managed up to three consultants with regular one-to-ones and performance reviews.

Genuine EDI credibility through Tate's EDI strategy team and co-founding an inclusive leadership network.

Apprenticeship recruitment experience, including levy conversations with employers and sustained work with Amazing Apprenticeships.

Daily ATS ownership with responsibility for data integrity, right-to-work checks, referencing and GDPR compliance.

PSL and agency-side supplier management experience, giving a client-side view of cost control.

Proven pipeline-building and sourcing strategy from scratch, including social media and events.

Budget and P&L ownership at scale, having run a £36 million food and beverage budget across 72 sites.

Development areas & cherries on top

Gap: No direct Dayforce experience

You've named this gap yourself rather than glossing over it, which is the right move. Before the interview, spend an hour looking at Dayforce's own product overview or a walkthrough of its recruiting and onboarding module so you can speak to its structure specifically, then frame your answer around how quickly you mastered Tate's ATS daily for nine years as evidence of how fast you'll pick this up too.

Gap: In-house recruitment versus agency-side delivery

Your whole career has been agency-side at Tate, while this role sits inside a single small in-house team of two. In the interview, get specific about the difference: talk about how you'd build ongoing relationships with the same hiring managers over years rather than transactional briefs, and how you'd apply the PSL management insight from being on the other side of that fence.

Gap: No formal HR or CIPD qualification

The job description lists CIPD Level 5 as desirable rather than essential, so this shouldn't block you, but naming a concrete plan will help. Mention that you're either already looking into or willing to start a CIPD Level 5 or equivalent qualification in your first year.

Gap: Employer brand and marketing-led attraction campaigns

The role wants you to work with Marketing on careers content and outreach like Theatrecraft and job fairs. Draw directly on your Account Director years at LAW Creative and your Marketing Manager role at Awards International, and connect that explicitly to what employer brand content for the Hall would need.

Gap: Recruitment within a charity or cultural/heritage sector context

Your recruitment career has been entirely within a commercial recruitment agency and hospitality, not the arts, charity or heritage world the Hall operates in. Use your genuine personal connection as a working musician who already loves the building to bridge this.

09 · STAR Answers

Sample Predicted Questions

These are illustrative answers built to show the format - your report builds these from your own recorded or typed answers, tidied into a clean, tellable story.

"A hiring manager in Philanthropy wants a bespoke, high-touch selection process while you're mid-way through a high-volume seasonal campaign for Visitor Services with the same two-person team - how do you decide where your time actually goes that week?"

Based on: delivering high-volume and complex campaigns simultaneously, two-person team
S
At Tate, right in the middle of a summer graduate recruitment surge with over 40 roles live at once, a senior Development hiring manager needed a highly bespoke, multi-stage process for a major-donor-facing role.
T
I was responsible for delivering both simultaneously with no extra headcount.
A
I triaged by risk and reversibility: the seasonal roles had a wide, forgiving candidate pool, so I built a lightweight, templated process I could run largely on autopilot, then blocked protected time for the bespoke hire and set clear weekly expectations with both hiring managers.
R
Both roles were filled inside their target timelines, the bespoke hire in nine weeks against a role that had previously taken four months, and I didn't lose a single seasonal requisition to slow process.

"What does 'good' look like when you're coaching a hiring manager who keeps defaulting to the same job board and the same shortlist profile they've always used?"

Based on: shaping inclusive attraction, challenging assumptions, coaching hiring managers
S
One hiring manager at Tate consistently asked for the same job board and near-identical shortlist profile for every creative role, regardless of the brief.
T
My job was to broaden the candidate pool without simply overriding them.
A
Rather than telling them the approach was wrong, I ran one role as an experiment: sourced a parallel shortlist using different channels and broader transferable-skills criteria, then presented both shortlists side by side so they could compare quality themselves.
R
The manager chose two candidates from the broadened shortlist, one was hired, and they adopted the wider sourcing approach as their default for the next eight roles I ran for them.

"How would you go about controlling agency spend on a hard-to-fill specialist role without just quietly letting time-to-hire slip instead?"

Based on: managing recruitment budgets and agency spend for value for money
S
A specialist technical role sat unfilled for six weeks with an agency on a flat-percentage fee and limited results.
T
I needed to bring cost down without the role drifting further.
A
I renegotiated the agency's terms to a capped, tiered fee tied to time-to-hire, and in parallel built a direct-sourcing campaign of my own running alongside them, so I wasn't solely dependent on the agency to move the role forward.
R
The role was filled three weeks later through my own direct sourcing, at roughly 40% of the original agency fee, and I used the renegotiated terms as the template for two other hard-to-fill briefs that quarter.

"Walk me through how you'd set up new starter data entry so that what recruitment captures actually lands cleanly in HR and payroll without someone having to fix it later."

Based on: accountable for quality and accuracy of new starter data flow into HR systems
S
At Tate, new starter data moving from our ATS into HR and payroll was error-prone - right-to-work dates and referencing sign-off were sometimes keyed in twice, and mistakes were only caught after someone had already started.
T
I was accountable for the accuracy of that handover for every hire I made.
A
I built a single-page new starter checklist that had to be fully signed off inside the ATS before a requisition could be marked "hired," and worked with HR to agree exactly which fields they needed pulled through so nothing was re-keyed by hand.
R
New starter data errors reaching payroll on my requisitions dropped close to zero, and two other consultants adopted the same checklist.

"If a hiring manager complains that your standard selection process is slowing them down for a role they consider urgent, how do you decide whether to hold the line on process or adapt it?"

Based on: designing fair, effective selection processes while supporting fast-paced hiring managers
S
A hiring manager pushed back hard on a two-stage interview process for an urgent Marketing hire, wanting to skip straight to an offer after one informal chat.
T
I had to protect a fair, consistent process without losing the hiring manager's confidence or the candidate.
A
I agreed to compress the timeline rather than cut a stage, running both interviews within 72 hours instead of the usual two weeks, and was transparent with the hiring manager about why the second stage mattered.
R
The process still ran in under a week, the candidate accepted, and the hiring manager asked me to run the same compressed-but-complete model for their next urgent hire rather than skipping stages again.
10 · Your Questions

Sharp, Specific, Grounded In Research

Type 1 · About the company

The pack mentions increasing the number of global majority headliners and younger performers on stage, and creating new opportunities for diverse participants across the Hall team more broadly. How far has that ambition already translated into changes in who applies for roles here, versus who's actually getting hired?

The Hall talks about being a Force For Good and reviewing recruitment strategies to widen the candidate pool - is there a specific department or role type where that widening has proven hardest, and where you'd want this role to focus first?

Type 2 · About the job

This is a newly created position sitting in a two-person team, with the expectation that I'd cover day-to-day admin when my colleague is off. Practically speaking, how is the workload split right now between strategic work and hands-on casework, and does that shift a lot during seasonal peaks?

You mention partnering with the Systems Officer and Senior People Partner to make sure the ATS supports compliant recruitment, and separately maintaining working knowledge of Dayforce for data flow into payroll. Where are the current gaps or pain points between those two systems that you'd want fixed first?

Type 3 · About the interviewers

Since this role reports to you directly, what prompted the decision to create this position now rather than continuing to run recruitment the way it's currently structured?

You'll have seen recruitment run across everything from Philanthropy to Building Services to Visitor Services - which of those functions currently gets the least consistent recruitment experience, and where would you want to see the first improvement land?

Type 4 · About you, in this role

Based on our conversation so far, is there anything you'd like me to clarify about my fit for this role?
